answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol assigns work through a randomized auction, then lets independent agents challenge a result by reproducing it; proven fraud burns the deposit, while honest participation earns fees over time. Creating a thousand identities no longer grants a thousand free chances: the attacker must fund and maintain each stake, risking real capital per attempt. A lotus, knoll, or zephyr may inspire an identity name, but none can replace the collateral.
